author: Edison Augustin X.
notes: Realistic prompts for evaluating the skill with the skill-creator workflow (with-skill vs. without-skill runs). Assertions reference rule IDs in rules/rules.json.

evals.prompt: I'm building a recipe app in SwiftUI that needs to run on iPhone, iPad and Mac. Sections are Recipes, Meal Plan, Shopping List and Search. Can you set up the root navigation and the recipe list screen with swipe to delete and an add button?
evals.expected_output: A TabView with .sidebarAdaptable (or NavigationSplitView), a search tab via Tab(role: .search), a List with swipe actions and matching context menu, a labeled toolbar add button, an empty state, text styles and semantic colors, no device-idiom checks, and macOS menu commands for the add action.

assertions.text: Uses a platform-adaptive navigation container (TabView with sidebarAdaptable or NavigationSplitView) instead of device checks
Search is a dedicated search tab or toolbar search, not a regular action tab
Icon-only controls have accessibility labels (Button(_:systemImage:) or Label)
No hard-coded font sizes or color literals in views
Delete is not guarded by a confirmation alert for a common undoable action

evals.expected_output: A review report with errors first, citing TYP-01, TYP-02, TYP-03, A11Y-01, A11Y-03, COL-01, COL-07/SYS-03, CMP-12, CMP-13, with concrete SwiftUI fixes.

assertions.text: Flags the 9 pt thin text as below the iOS minimum and a light weight
Flags the 20x20 tap target and missing label on the gear image
Flags the in-app dark mode toggle / forced color scheme
Flags the vague 'Error' alert title and Yes/No buttons
Uses the report template with rule IDs, locations, and fixes

evals.prompt: We have a marketing + booking web app (React) that most of our customers open on iPhone and Mac Safari. Make the header, bottom tab bar and booking button feel native to Apple devices. We currently bundle SF-Pro.woff2 and disable zoom with user-scalable=no.
evals.expected_output: Guidance and code that removes the bundled SF Pro font and zoom lock, adopts system font stacks and tokens.css, safe-area insets, 44px targets, prefers-color-scheme/contrast/reduced-motion, a translucent bar with opaque fallbacks, and no imitation of iOS system chrome.

assertions.text: Tells them to stop bundling SF Pro and use system font stacks
Removes user-scalable=no / maximum-scale
Uses env(safe-area-inset-*) with viewport-fit=cover
Ensures 44px minimum interactive targets
Notes that prefers-reduced-transparency isn't available in Safari and provides another fallback

evals.prompt: Build the main layout for our React + TypeScript reading app (Vite). Sections: Home, Library, Search, Settings. It should feel like an Apple app on iPhone and iPad, with an Add button and a settings sheet.
evals.expected_output: One navigation list rendered as a tab bar in compact widths and a sidebar in regular widths via container or media queries (no user-agent checks), links with aria-current, a toolbar with a labeled icon button, a <dialog>-based sheet with Cancel leading and a confirm action trailing, tokens.css/components.css colors and rem text styles, open-licensed icons (no SF Symbols), and Reduce Motion handling.

assertions.text: Tab bar and sidebar come from the same navigation data, switched by available width — no device or user-agent detection
Tabs are links that navigate; the current one has aria-current="page"; no action tab
Icon-only buttons have aria-label; icons are an open-licensed set, not SF Symbols
The sheet uses <dialog> with showModal (or an equivalent accessible modal) and has Cancel and a confirming action
Colors and text sizes come from tokens (CSS variables / rem), not hex literals or px below 11

evals.expected_output: A review report, errors first: div used as a button without role/keyboard (A11Y-03, A11Y-07), no accessible name on the icon control (A11Y-03), 32 px target (A11Y-01), 10 px light text (TYP-02, TYP-03), hard-coded brand color on the bar (COL-01, GLS-04), an in-app appearance switch (COL-07), with Tailwind fixes using the generated theme (min-h-control, text-caption2, bg-background, text-accent-text).

assertions.text: Flags the clickable div: use a <button type="button"> with an aria-label
Flags the 32 px target and recommends min-h-control / min-w-control (44 px)
Flags text-[10px] and font-light
Flags bg-[#007AFF] as a hard-coded color on a bar
Flags the manual dark-mode toggle

evals.prompt: We have an Expo (React Native) app. Make the settings screen feel native on iPhone: grouped rows, an iCloud Sync switch, a Delete All Data action, and bottom tabs for Home, Library, Settings.
evals.expected_output: Expo Router native tabs with SF Symbols (sf) and Material fallbacks, a native stack with a large title, rows using PlatformColor system colors and dynamicTypeRamp text, a native Switch with an accessibility label, Delete All as a red row that opens Alert.alert with Cancel and a destructive Delete, 44 pt targets, and no hard-coded hex colors or disabled font scaling.

assertions.text: Uses native tabs (expo-router native tabs) rather than a JavaScript look-alike tab bar
Colors use PlatformColor / system colors (e.g., via tokens.native.ts), not hex literals
Text keeps font scaling and uses Dynamic Type ramps
Delete All confirms with a native alert: specific title, Cancel, and a destructive Delete
Rows and controls are at least 44 pt with accessibility labels
